title: The Church as a Spiritual Spring Meadow
english: When the season of spring succeeds the gloom of winter, birds of every kind fly through the bright air and signal the sweetness of the season to human beings with honey-voiced songs. Then the sweet-singing swallows cut through the air with swift flight, dart past people's heads, and cast their own cry into human ears like a flower. Then one can see the air clear and calm, and people's faces bright, reshaped in imitation of the stillness. For the voices of birds delight the hearing, the clear air brightens the eye, the gleam of many-colored flowers sweetens the sight, and the mingled breath of the plants restores the sense of smell.

This is the delight that the earthly and perishable spring offers to human beings, beloved. But our divine and incorruptible spring, Christ, has thickly covered the meadow of the church with violets and roses and spiritual lilies, and he brightens our sight with faith and fills the reservoir of our heart with divine spices. For which of the faithful does not rejoice now? Who does not exult now, seeing the newly baptized shining in the image of lilies with the bright calyxes of their robes, and possessing the gold-gleaming faith in the middle of the heart?

Here you will find, beloved, if you gaze with the eyes of the heart, the heart of the faithful dyed purple like a deepest violet with the blood of Jesus. For the flame-leaved rose has blossomed incorruptibly from the virgin Mary. What meadow possesses such fragrance as our meadow, which perfumes the grace of the Spirit? Inhale the newly baptized, and you will find in them the immortal fragrance of the Spirit—I mean the myrrh of the heavenly anointing.

Here the palms of the fathers, crowned with the victory branches, bear sweeter fruits of love, fragrant as cypress. Here the beautiful-voiced birds of the psalmists sing the psalms to God in harmony on the lyre. Here virginity, like storax offering the pure incense of prayer to God, rejoices. Here self-control, sacrificing the cheerful branch of purity to God as Abraham offered Isaac, takes delight. Here the trunks of mercy, putting forth the fruitful branch of good deeds to the poor, delight the Lord and nourish the needy.

Let virginity sing and say: "Let my prayer be set before you as incense, Lord" (Psalm 141:2). Let the merciful say: "But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God" (Psalm 52:8 (LXX 51:10)). For the righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and will be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon (Psalm 92:12-13 (LXX 91:13-14)).

Now the gloom of the devil's winter has fled, and the cheerful radiance of the heavenly meadow has shone forth. Now the mourning of the dead has run away, for the light of the resurrection has come. Let us all sing together the new song, for the new and blessed song befits the new way of life. Let us sing the new song, for behold, Adam has been renewed, the old sin has been destroyed, behold, all things have become new.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, opens his homily on the newly baptized by comparing the church to a spring meadow filled with spiritual flowers and fragrance.
